question: Do bounded buckets reduce edit time and maintained position-index work versus a flat ordered array with a key-to-index Map?
claimBoundary: Data-structure evidence only. No component owner, compiler graph, JSX, VDOM, DOM, React, layout, paint, or frame behavior is measured.

workload.operation: move an existing keyed row before a stable anchor

arms.indexed-array: Map key lookup plus Array.splice; after each splice, update key-to-index entries for every row in the shifted suffix
arms.bucketed: KeyedRegionBuckets Map key lookup plus bounded bucket-local splice and position reindex

measures: final ordered key equality and bucket integrity
analysis: Report per-sample median and nearest-rank p95 by size, locality, arm, and bucket capacity. Keep position-index rewrites and bucket-slot movement distinct; do not equate unlike implementation counters. Verify exact final order after timing.
knownLimitations: The index map must be updated for all positions affected by Array.splice; this is the standard cost of preserving direct key-to-index lookup in a flat array.
Counters are logical maintenance operations, not bytes allocated, cache misses, or total engine work.
Seven measured samples make nearest-rank p95 the maximum and cannot characterize a stable tail.
